description: Obiectivele acestui contract sunt: Realizarea unui imobil nou, modern, adaptat cerintelor actuale ale domeniului muzeal si capabil sa sustina in conditii optime activitati culturale, stiintifice si recreative, prin edificarea unei cladiri contemporane, dotate corespunzator si integrate armonios in contextul urban si natural al Parcului Monument, urmarindu-se reafirmarea Colectiei de Stiinte ale Naturii a Muzeului Brailei ,,Carol I” ca reper cultural local si regional. Etapa I - Elaborare documentatie proiectare: a) Documentatie tehnica (D.T.A.C + D.T.O.E), pentru autorizarea executarii lucrarilor de construire si pentru autorizarea executarii organizarii lucrarilor; b) Proiect Tehnic (P.T) + Detalii de executie (D.E) + Caiete de sarcini (C.S); c) Documentatie As built; d) Elaborare documentatie tehnica necesara obtinerii autorizatiei de securitate la incendiu, in termen de 10 zile de la receptia la terminarea lucrarilor; e) Certificat energetic – anexa la procesul verbal de receptie la terminarea lucrarilor; f) Elaborare analiza de risc, proiectarea si obtinerea Avizului Inspectoratului Judetean de Politie privind executia sistemului de supraveghere video; -Etapa II - Asigurarea asistenței tehnice incepand cu procedura achizitiei pentru contractul de executie lucrari, pe perioada executiei lucrarilor si pana la admiterea receptiei la terminarea lucrarilor respectiv admiterea receptiei finale. Numărul de zile până la care se pot solicita clarificări înainte de data limită de depunere a ofertelor este de 18 zile. Autoritatea contractantă va răspunde în mod clar și complet tuturor solicitărilor de clarificare/informațiilor suplimentare în a 11-a zi înainte de termenul limită stabilit de depunere a ofertelor. Termenul de răspuns la clarificări nu afectează dreptul operatorilor economici interesați de a transmite solicitări de clarificare pe parcursul întregii perioade cuprinse între momentul publicării anunțului de participare și până la termenul-limită prevăzut pentru transmiterea solicitărilor de clarificare: cu 18 zile calendaristice anterior termenului-limită de primire a ofertelor stabilit de autoritatea contractantă. Întrucât autoritatea contractantă are obligația de a răspunde în mod clar și complet tuturor solicitărilor de clarificări, trebuie să își aloce un termen rezonabil pentru analiza solicitărilor de clarificări și formularea răspunsurilor. Conform art. 160 din Legea nr. 98/2016 cu modificarile si completarile ulterioare, obligatia autoritatii contractante de a raspunde la solicitarile de clarificari este conditionata de transmiterea solicitarilor de clarificare in termenul impus prin documentatia de atribuire, a se tine cont in acest caz de termenul indicat la I.3.

title: Educational Services
description: An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. As per the Commissioner’s Directive 720 (Education Programs and Services for Offenders), when an inmate's grade level is below grade 12 or its provincial equivalent, education will be identified as a need in their Correctional Plan. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to: a. Facilitate inmates' reintegration by increasing educational skill levels through the provision of accredited programs. b. Ensure education programs and library services respect gender, ethnic, cultural and linguistic differences, and are responsive to the special needs of women inmates, Indigenous inmates, inmates requiring mental health care and other groups. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: To provide educational services to the inmates at Nova Institution for Women. 1.2 Tasks: 1 The Contractor must provide the following resources: a. Two (2) teachers/instructors who must provide teaching services - 35 hours per week at 7 hours per day - Monday to Friday 2 The Contractor must deliver the following educational services: a. Adult Basic Education program (ABE); b. Adapted ABE programs for offenders with learning difficulties and disabilities; c. Educational programs leading to the Adult High School Diploma; d. Other education programs, pilot programs, digital education and any other curriculum the Project Authority requests; e. Coordination of post-secondary pre-requisite courses, correspondence courses and other programs including but not limited to, the Walls to Bridges program; f. Provide appropriate provincially recognized certificates, following course and level completions. 3. One (1) of the certified teachers must be designated as Lead teacher to: a. Ensure bilingual educational services at the school, in the Secure Unit (SU) and in the Structured Intervention Unit (SIU); b. Establish and coordinate schedules for the teachers/instructors; c. Ensure teachers/instructors follow the prescribed provincial curriculum; d. Ensure teachers/instructors provide quality educational services to offenders; e. Maintain enrolments in education programs at full capacity; f. Teach and facilitate independent studies (cell studies); g. Review all incoming inmates’ education information and provide parole officers with data necessary to make referrals to education programs; h. Evaluate the inmates’ educational needs, waitlists and suspensions; i. Administer and score the Canadian Adult Achievement Test and the “Test de rendement pour francophones” or other assessment tools approved by the Project Authority; j. Offer educational counseling to students; k. Adjust and combine classes to ensure continuity of educational services to inmates, in the event of teacher/instructor absences; l. Perform other related tasks to ensure proper operation of the school; m. Submit requests to the Project Authority for the purchase of pedagogical resources and office/school supplies; n. Participate in the Correctional Interventions Board (CIB) meetings and provide information/recommendations; o. Follow the CIB guidelines in terms of assigning inmates based on the student-to-teacher ratio to maximize education program capacity; p. Collaborate with the CIB to assign inmates to the educational tutor positions. The Contractor must work in collaboration with CSC to hire inmate classroom tutors. This must include in classroom training and orientation of the tutor by the contract teacher/instructor; q. Collaborate with the Volunteer Coordinator to assign volunteer community tutors to the classrooms; r. Participate in meetings as requested by the Project Authority; s. Supervise contract teachers/instructors, monitor and coordinate visits relative to the education programs; t. Participate in the yearly development of the annual education program plan (AEPP); u. Assist the Project Authority with input, data analysis, and reporting, as it relates to the educational results, prior learning assessment and recognition (PLAR) credits, progress, forecasting, curriculum development, digital programs, pilot programs, and digital education; v. Ensure an efficient information-sharing process such as e-mails pertaining to work safety, security reminders, and general information which is deemed necessary to inform personnel and to maintain a safe and secure environment; w. Organize and invigilate Canadian Adult Education Credential (CAEC) testing sessions and other assessments in both official languages, which may take place during the evening or during institutional operational hours; x. Always ensure, that resources, services, and communication are available in both official languages; y. Ensure that all communication and information is sent to all institutional staff in both official languages and pre-approved by the Project Authority or the Program Manager. 4. Contract teachers/instructors must: a. Provide individualized teaching and education plans; b. Assess the academic needs and aptitudes of inmates; c. Ensure inventory control of CSC assets always related to education programs; d. Provide a variety of teaching strategies (including, but not limited to individualized learning, group learning, guests’ presentations); e. Employ classroom management techniques and methods to ensure the protection and preservation of educational resources (including, but not limited to books, supplies, equipment); f. Complete daily visual searches of the installations before and after each teaching sessions; g. Complete observation reports and immediately submit to CSC security personnel any information or observations of incidents that could jeopardize the safety or the security of others. This may include charging inmates for various infractions; h. Supervise and evaluate the inmate cleaner in the school area according to CD-730 “Offender Program Assignment and Inmate Payments”; i. Collaborate with the Volunteer Coordinator to guide and monitor the community volunteer tutors in the classroom; j. Prepare and take steps to recognize significant cultural dates and months by providing presentations, collages, and other forms of visual reminders to staff and inmates throughout the school; k. Cooperate and collaborate with CSC management, staff, and other contractors. 1.3 Expected results: Provision of education services to enable inmates to achieve grade 12 or its provincial equivalent. 1.4 Performance standards: 1. The Contractor must ensure that the contract teachers/instructors understand and adhere to the following CSC policies, guidelines and procedures: a. CD 001 - Mission, Values and Ethics Framework of the Correctional Service of Canada : https://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/acts-and-regulations/001-cd-en.shtml b. CSC Policy (Commissioner Directives and Standard Operating Practices) and Legislation: https://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/acts-and-regulations/005006-0001-en.shtml i. CD 350: Contracting and Material Management ii. CD 568-1: Recording and Reporting of Security Incidents iii. CD 577: Staff Protocol in Women Offender Institutions iv. CD 701: Information Sharing v. CD 720: Education Programs and Services for Offenders vi. CD 720-1: Guidelines for Education Programs vii. CD 730: Offender Program Assignments and Inmate Payments viii. CD 764: Access to Materials ix. Program Strategy for Federally Sentenced Women x. C

title: Bruker VERTEX NEO Ultra Fourier-transform Infrared Vacuum Spectrometer
description: The objective of this purchase is to acquire a high-performance research-grade Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer capable of advanced infrared spectroscopic measurements across the mid-IR and far-IR regions, with high spectral resolution, vacuum optics, time-resolved measurement capability, multiple detector/source configurations, and flexible sample/accessory compatibility. The system will support demanding R&D applications, including high-resolution spectral analysis, rapid-scan and step-scan experiments, far-IR measurements, reflectance/transmission/ATR measurements, and data acquisition, processing, validation, reporting, and management through integrated spectroscopy software

title: Stream to Sea Program Delivery and Coordination Services: South Coast – Victoria, Sooke, Saanich and Southern Gulf Islands
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) Solicitation #: 30008053 This requirement is for Fisheries and Oceans Canada Title: Stream to Sea Program Delivery and Coordination Services: South Coast – Victoria, Sooke, Saanich and Southern Gulf Islands Objective: Fisheries and Oceans Canada, requires Contractors to provide delivery and coordination services for the Stream to Sea Program, as defined by the Project Authority, for schools within School Districts listed below, as well as Independent Schools, other Learning Centres, and community partners in the same geographic area: Victoria, Sooke, Saanich and Southern Gulf Islands (including School Districts (SD) 61, 62, 63, 64) Stream to Sea Program delivery and coordination services are required over the entire duration of this Contract with some times requiring more commitment than others. Delivery and coordination services will be defined on a geographic specific basis through the development of work plan details using the information provided in Appendix 1 (Scope of Work). The Contractor will work with the Project Authority, to coordinate and deliver the Stream to Sea Program in schools and with local community groups. The work will consist of training educators, coordinating and assisting with set up of classroom incubators (aquaria), delivering salmon eggs to schools, providing classroom (indoor and outdoor) sessions which may include the salmon life cycle, fish dissections, aquatic ecosystems and habitat requirements for salmon, environmental sustainability as it relates to salmon, stream to sea migration and other salmon focused education pertinent to the area. The Contractor will provide trouble shooting and maintenance support for aquaria in schools and develop or assist with the development and delivery of a spring fry release program for participating schools. In some instances, the Contractor may participate in the live transport of adult and juvenile salmon and may participate in the spawning of broodstock. Contractor will also support Pacific Region tracking and reporting (i.e. brood stock summary and year end stream to sea data collection/reporting). The Stream to Sea Program aims to develop opportunities for external parties to be involved. Contractors may be required to facilitate and develop opportunities with local communities, First Nations, and community groups. Security Requirement: There is no security associated with this requirement. Period of Contract: The period of contract shall be from date of award to July 31, 2028. There are three (3) option periods of one (1) year to be exercised at the discretion of the Department. description: Trade Agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) Canada–Chile Free Trade Agreement Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) Canada–Colombia Free Trade Agreement Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) Canada–Honduras Free Trade Agreement Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement Canada–Peru Free Trade Agreement Canada–Ukraine Free Trade Agreement Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement World Trade Organization–Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA) Tendering Procedures: Selective tendering – Request for proposal against a supply arrangement to pre-qualified suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: The bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory technical evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid achieving the highest Total Financial Score will be recommended for award of a contract. The financial evaluation will be conducted using a weighted financial point-rated methodology. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: No. Nature of Requirements: Name of the requirement: Acquisition of a High-Performance Liquid Chromatography with Electrochemical Detection (HPLC-ECD) Suite Reference number: 5000093004 Email: solicitation-demandedesoumission@cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca THIS REQUEST IS RESERVED FOR HOLDERS OF SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT # E60PV-19EQUI ONLY, FOR THE PURCHASE OF LABORATORY AND SCIENTIFIC EQUIPMENT, PARTS AND ACCESSORIES, SERVICES AND SUPPLIES. Only Suppliers currently pre-qualified on Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI have been invited to bid. As a requirement of the Supply Arrangement, this notice is published on Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) for a period of 40 calendar days. The closing date published on this notice identifies how long the notice will be published. For the closing date of any solicitation under the supply arrangement, invited suppliers should refer to the solicitation documents. Suppliers that do not have a Supply Arrangement for the supply of Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies with Public Works and Government Services Canada, cannot submit a bid. Any bids received from suppliers not pre-qualified on the Supply Arrangement will not be evaluated. Suppliers may qualify under Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI for Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies, at any time. Interested suppliers should download solicitation document E60PV-19EQUI/D from CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba) and submit a response as per the requirements of the Request for Supply Arrangement. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) Laboratory has a requirement to acquire a liquid chromatography system coupled with an electrochemical detector for the analysis of trace amounts of hydrazine and morpholine in fresh water samples. These components, collectively title the HPLC-ECD suite will employ high-performance liquid chromatography techniques to separate the hydrazine and morpholine from its sample matrix, and analyze their concentrations via amperometry using an electrochemical detector. The mandatory technical criteria are included in Annex A. The responsive bidder already holding a Supply arrangement for Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies from Public Works and Government Services Canada who meets the mandatory technical criteria with the highest Total Financial Score will be recommended for contract award.

description: Kaivokselan koulu korjaus ja tilamuutokset Hankinta käsittää Kaivokselan koulun perusparannus –hankkeen rakennusurakan / pääurakan työt urakkalaskenta-asiakirjojen mukaisesti. Työt tehdään tilaajan laadituttamien suunnitelmien mukaan. Rakennusurakoitsija toimii pääurakoitsijana. Tilaaja hankkii pääurakkaan alistettavina sivu-urakoina: putki-, ilmanvaihto-, sähkö- ja rakennusautomaatiourakat. Rakennusurakoitsija toimii myös urakan ajan kohteen päätoteuttajana sekä työmaan johtovelvollisuuksista ja työmaapalveluista vastaavana urakoitsijana. Urakkakilpailu toteutetaan avoimella menettelyllä. Tilaaja on tarjouspyynnössä määrittänyt tarjoajalta vaadittavat kelpoisuus- /soveltuvuusehdot. Halvimman (vertailuhinta) tarjouksen antanut kelpoisuusehdot täyttävä urakoitsija valitaan pääurakoitsijaksi. Vuonna 1966 valmistuneeseen koulurakennukseen tehdään sisäpuolinen peruskorjaus ja kohteen piha-alueelle tehdään muutoksia. Isoimpina muutoksia pintarakenteiden uusimisien lisäksi ovat mm. ruokasalin ja keittiön uusiminen toiseen sijaintiin rakennuksessa, kahden hissin rakentaminen, katolla olevien IV-konehuoneiden laajennukset koneineen sekä alapohjarakenteiden uusimiset suunnitelmien mukaan ja purunpoistotilan laajennus. Koulu ei ole käytössä rakentamisen aikana. Rakennuskohteen nimi: Kaivokselan koulu korjaus ja tilamuutokset Kaivosvoudintie 10 01610 Vantaa,

title: Aviapoliksen lukion ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta
description: Aviapoliksen lukion ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta Vantaan kaupungin Aviapoliksen lukiolle tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Aviapoliksen lukio otetaan käyttöön asteittain. Alkuvaiheessa vuonna 2027 opiskelijoita arvioidaan olevan 90 opiskelijaa. Henkilökuntaa arvioidaan olevan alkuvaiheessa noin 2-15 henkilöä. Vuonna 2028 oppilasmäärän arvioidaan olevan noin 530 ja henkilökuntaa noin 15-20 henkilöä ja vuonna 2029 oppilasmäärä on arviolta 700 oppilasta. Vuoden 2029 tarkkaa henkilökuntamäärää ei vielä ole tiedossa. Tilaaja valitsee enintään yhden (1) sopimustoimittajan. Sopimus tehdään toistaiseksi voimassa olevaksi. Sopimuksen ehdot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevissa sopimusluonnoksissa (liite 1 ja 2). Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.1.2027. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa arvioituihin hankintamääriin tai euromääräisiin arvoihin sopimuskaudella. Tarjoajien tarjouksien määrittelemisen helpottamiseksi, Tilaaja järjestää kohteeseen yhteisnäyttöpäivän. Tarjoajien on osallistuttava yhteisnäyttöpäivään, ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Tarjouspyynnön kohteena olevat tilat ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden osalta esitellään seuraavasti: Aviapoliksen lukio, 26.10.2026 klo 9.00 Kohteen tilojen esittelytilaisuuksiin tulee ilmoittautua viimeistään 23.10.2026 klo 16.00 mennessä sähköpostitse osoitteeseen ostoyksikko.puhtauspalvelut@vantaa.fi. Tarjoajien tasapuolisen ja syrjimättömän kohtelun vuoksi tarjoajien kohteissa esittämiin kysymyksiin ei vastata. Kaikki yhteisnäyttökierroksilla esiin tulleet kysymykset tulee esittää tarjouspalvelu.fi:n kautta, jonka kautta annetaan myös vastaukset tulleisiin kysymyksiin. Tarjoajan tulee todistaa henkilöllisyys osallistuessaan yhteisnäyttöön. Lisätietoja yhteisnäyttöpäivästä löytyy kohdasta Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit.,

title: Reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service
description: Reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service Gasgrid Finland Oy (hereinafter “Contracting Authority”) is a state-owned gas transmission system operator (TSO) that started operating in early 2020. The company mission is to ensure cost-effective, safe and undisturbed gas transmission and to actively develop the gas market and the Finnish energy system. The company has the overall system responsibility for the entire methane gas transmission network in Finland. The Contracting Authority is planning to construct a natural gas compression station to Lempäälä, Finland. Construction work is scheduled to be started approx. Q2/2027. Installation of the compressor unit(s) is planned to be started approx. Q2/2028. The schedule mentioned is indicative and subject to changes. In this procurement the Contracting Authority is looking for a supplier for 2+1 (option) complete, electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service to Gasgrid’s Lempäälä gas compression station. The key specifications as follows (but not limited to these): - Each compressor package shall comprise one electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor unit, together with the associated process equipment, auxiliaries, electrical equipment, instrumentation, control and safety systems, and other equipment necessary to provide a complete, safe and operable compressor package suitable for integration into the Compressor Station. - The Supplier shall be responsible for the design, manufacture, testing, documentation, delivery, integration and conformity of the complete compressor package within the final agreed scope of supply. The Supplier shall also be responsible for defining and managing the necessary technical and safety interfaces between the compressor package and systems or equipment supplied by the Contracting Authority, EPCM Contractor or other parties, to the extent necessary for the safe integration and conformity of the compressor package. - The anticipated operating envelope of each compressor unit is approximately 3,000 Nm³/h, with suction pressure approximately 4–8 barg and discharge pressure up to approximately 54 barg. -The compressor packages shall comply with all applicable European Union and Finnish legislation and requirements, including the applicable requirements of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex V, Part A – Declaration of Conformity for Completed Machinery, PED 2014/68/EU, ATEX 2014/34/EU and EMC 2014/30/EU. -The Supplier shall be capable of fulfilling the applicable manufacturer obligations and conformity assessment requirements for the complete compressor package, including provision of the required declarations, CE marking and conformity documentation. Site supervision and commissioning support, including support for the required on-site conformity and CE marking activities, are included. Installation at site is excluded from the scope of supply. Detailed technical requirements, operating conditions, performance requirements, scope boundaries, interfaces and documentation requirements will be defined in the procurement documentation issued during the subsequent phase of the procurement procedure.,

title: Taidetestaajat-ohjelmahaku kaudelle 2027–28
description: Taidetestaajat-ohjelmahaku kaudelle 2027–28 Hankinnan kohteena ovat Taidetestaajat-ohjelmaan lukuvuodelle 2027–2028 valittavien taide- ja kulttuurisisältöjen (sis. yleisötyö) pääsyliput. Taidetestaajat on valtakunnallinen kulttuurikasvatusohjelma, joka tarjoaa kaikille Suomen kahdeksasluokkalaisille mahdollisuuden osallistua korkeatasoiseen taiteeseen ja kulttuuriin osana koulupäivää. Lukuvuonna 2027–2028 tavoitteena on toteuttaa yksi taidevierailu kullekin ohjelmaan osallistuvalle kouluryhmälle. Hankinta kattaa eri taiteenaloja, kuten teatteria, musiikkia, tanssia, sirkusta, oopperaa, kuvataidetta, museoita ja elokuvaa. Hankittavien palvelujen tulee soveltua kahdeksasluokkalaisille ja sisältää taidekokemukseen liittyvää pedagogista materiaalia tai muuta etukäteis- ja jälkikäsittelyä tukevaa sisältöä. Ohjelmaan osallistuu vuosittain noin 70 000 henkeä, 8.-luokan oppilasta sekä heidän opettajiaan ja muita valvojiaan. Hankinnan arvioitu kokonaisarvo on noin 1,4 miljoonaa euroa arvonlisäveroineen. Hankinta jakautuu useille eri taide- ja kulttuuriorganisaatioille eri puolilla Suomea. Hankittavien pääsylippujen määrät ja jakautuminen eri tuotantoihin määräytyvät lopullisten ohjelmistovalintojen, koulujen osallistumisen ja käytettävissä olevan rahoituksen perusteella. Hankinnan toteutuminen edellyttää riittävän julkisen rahoituksen varmistumista.,

title: Anskaffelsesbistand til Forsvarsmateriell
description: Forsvarsmateriell (FMA) har tre hovedoppgaver: å anskaffe, forvalte og utfase materiell for Forsvaret og øvrige virksomheter i forsvarssektoren. Målet er å gi Forsvaret raskere reaksjonsevne, høyere beredskap og lengere utholdenhet. FMA Anskaffelser inngår, forvalter, gjør avrop på rammeavtaler og inngår kontrakter på/anskaffer materiell i henhold til lov og forskrift om offentlige anskaffelser (LOA/FOA/FOSA) samt interne instrukser. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å inngå avtale med leverandører som kan bistå oppdragsgiver med gjennomføringen av anskaffelser. Bistanden skal dekke alle deler av anskaffelsesprosessen, herunder planlegging utarbeidelse av konkurransegrunnlag, gjennomføring av konkurranse, evaluering av tilbud, samt kontraktsinngåelse og for enkelte kategorier; kontraktsoppfølging. Det vises til SSA-B bilag 1 for nærmere angivelse av de ulike kategorienes omfang.

title: Finland – Gas compressors – Reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service
description: Gasgrid Finland Oy (hereinafter “Contracting Authority”) is a state-owned gas transmission system operator (TSO) that started operating in early 2020. The company mission is to ensure cost-effective, safe and undisturbed gas transmission and to actively develop the gas market and the Finnish energy system. The company has the overall system responsibility for the entire methane gas transmission network in Finland. The Contracting Authority is planning to construct a natural gas compression station to Lempäälä, Finland. Construction work is scheduled to be started approx. Q2/2027. Installation of the compressor unit(s) is planned to be started approx. Q2/2028. The schedule mentioned is indicative and subject to changes. In this procurement the Contracting Authority is looking for a supplier for 2+1 (option) complete, electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service to Gasgrid’s Lempäälä gas compression station. The key specifications as follows (but not limited to these): - Each compressor package shall comprise one electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor unit, together with the associated process equipment, auxiliaries, electrical equipment, instrumentation, control and safety systems, and other equipment necessary to provide a complete, safe and operable compressor package suitable for integration into the Compressor Station. - The Supplier shall be responsible for the design, manufacture, testing, documentation, delivery, integration and conformity of the complete compressor package within the final agreed scope of supply. The Supplier shall also be responsible for defining and managing the necessary technical and safety interfaces between the compressor package and systems or equipment supplied by the Contracting Authority, EPCM Contractor or other parties, to the extent necessary for the safe integration and conformity of the compressor package. - The anticipated operating envelope of each compressor unit is approximately 3,000 Nm³/h, with suction pressure approximately 4–8 barg and discharge pressure up to approximately 54 barg. -The compressor packages shall comply with all applicable European Union and Finnish legislation and requirements, including the applicable requirements of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex V, Part A – Declaration of Conformity for Completed Machinery, PED 2014/68/EU, ATEX 2014/34/EU and EMC 2014/30/EU. -The Supplier shall be capable of fulfilling the applicable manufacturer obligations and conformity assessment requirements for the complete compressor package, including provision of the required declarations, CE marking and conformity documentation. Site supervision and commissioning support, including support for the required on-site conformity and CE marking activities, are included. Installation at site is excluded from the scope of supply. Detailed technical requirements, operating conditions, performance requirements, scope boundaries, interfaces and documentation requirements will be defined in the procurement documentation issued during the subsequent phase of the procurement procedure.

title: Finland – Analysis apparatus – A light-scattering instrument for characterization of particles in liquid dispersions
description: Åbo Akademi University invites tenders for a complete light-scattering instrument system for research use. The procurement is planned as a national open procedure under the Finnish Act on Public Procurement and Concession Contracts (1397/2016). The procurement documents and tenders are handled electronically in Cloudia / HILMA as specified in the procurement notice. The object of the procurement is a light-scattering system suitable for characterizing liquid dispersions, suspensions, colloids, proteins, polymers, nanoparticles and comparable samples. The system must enable determination of particle size, zeta potential, molecular mass and particle concentration, together with automatic pH-dependent measurements. The tender shall cover a fully operational solution. All components, licences, cells, cuvettes, accessories, cables and other items required to perform the mandatory measurements must be included unless expressly identified as consumables or optional items in the tender.

title: 6515--Philips Lithium-Ion Batteries and Barcode Scanner
description: This RFI is solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government. Per FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not considered offers, shall not be used as a proposal, and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Neither unsolicited proposals nor any other kinds of offers will be considered in response to this notice. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents; however, the Government does reserve the right to contact any respondent and/or respondent reference to obtain additional information. At this time, no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. Any resulting procurement action will be the subject of a separate, future announcement. The information is provided for discussion purposes and any potential strategy for this acquisition may change prior to any solicitation release. The acquisition strategy, evaluation methodology, contract type, and any other acquisition decisions are to be determined. STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) Contract Title. Philips VS30 Batteries Background. Replacement: The DC VA Medical Center has a requirement to replace the existing Philips Medical VS30 Vital Signs batteries. The current VS30 vital signs batteries were purchased in 2025, have reached end of life, and are no longer usable. The VS30 battery life is 2 years and aligns with OEM preventative maintenance (PM) requirements. Only the VS30 vital signs monitors are being impacted, and the batteries must fully integrate with the existing Philips VS30 devices. Also requesting additional scanners for deployment and inventory. Scope of Work. The procurement shall include all parts, materials, labor, software/licenses, resources, and training required to implement and utilize the equipment/system to their fullest capacity. All items must be covered by manufacturer s warranty and procured through a manufacturer-approved distribution channel. Distributers and resellers must be able to document ability to provide items through manufacturer-approved distribution channels upon request. Specifications. 4.1 Equipment Line Item Description Quantity BATTERY PACK, 9-CELLS LITHIUM-ION, BLACK, 7.8AH CAPACITY, 11.1V VOLTAGE, FOR USE WITH: FOR VS30 EARLYVUE MONITOR by Philips / 989803199221 400 Periph HS-1 RFID Barcode Scanner (HS-1RS) / 989803225411 30 VSM roll stand barcode scanner holder / 989803210381 30 4.2 Required Features This battery must be the exact same as the BATTERY PACK, 9-CELLS LITHIUM-ION, BLACK, 7.8AH CAPACITY, 11.1V VOLTAGE, FOR USE WITH: FOR VS30 EARLYVUE MONITOR by Philips / 989803199221 to be compatible with the Philips VS30 Vital Signs monitor. Battery Capacity: 7.35 Ah Battery Chemistry: Lithium Ion Dimensions: 5.88 x 3.50 x 0.78 in Weight: 2.87 lbs Voltage: 11.1V The scanners must be the HS-1RS model to ensure compatibility and connectivity with active workflow and environment. Other scanners will require added costs, procedures, and networking which is not included in this package. Specific Tasks. 5.1 Delivery. All equipment shall be delivered to: Washington DC VA Medical Center 50 Irving St NW Washington, DC 20422 ATTN: VHAWAS Equipment Committee Contract VA Purchase Order (PO) number shall be included with delivery information (e.g., packing slip). Note: PO number starts with station code 688 followed by a letter and 5 digits (e.g., 688A12345) Delivery Hours: The Warehouse is open to receive deliveries Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., excluding holidays. Contractor shall coordinate delivery with the on-site Point of Contact (POC) and provide shipment tracking information. Contractor shall verify delivery date and time with the on-site POC at least 3 business days prior to scheduled delivery. Delivery is required within 90 days from award of the contract. 5.2 On Site Procedures. COVID-19 Screening: All persons entering the facility shall be subject to screening for COVID-19 per the current CDC (Center for Disease Control) guidelines. Mask Requirement: All contractors shall wear masks while indoors. Contract personnel are required to identify themselves as such to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government Officials. Time spent on site shall be for a period sufficient to complete the work set forth in the statement of work. On site visits shall be scheduled in advance with the designated on-site POC. Contractor shall check in and out with Biomedical Engineering prior to visiting the worksite for each day of work. The VA campus is non-smoking. Contractor personnel are required to comply with this policy. Parking: it is the responsibility of the Contractor to park in the appropriate designated parking areas. Contractor personnel s tool bags are subject to inspection. 5.3 Installation/Implementation. Installation/Implementation will be completed by personnel certified and knowledgeable with the designated equipment/system. Installation shall be completed within the period of performance. Contractor shall be responsible for any Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required when performing work on site. Contractor shall submit all removable media to be used on a VA system to Biomedical Engineering for scanning with anti-virus software prior to use. In the case turn-in, exchange, repair, or replacement of equipment containing hard drives used by the VA, the hard drives shall be removed from the equipment and remain in possession of the VA (this includes loaned or rented equipment). The contractor shall take all necessary precautions to prevent damage to any government property. The contractor shall report any damages immediately and shall be assessed current replacement costs for property damaged by the contractor, unless corrective action is taken. Any damaged material (i.e., trees, shrubs, lawn/turf, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, etc.) will be replaced in a timely manner or corrected by the contractor with like materials, at no extra cost to the government, upon approval of the Contracting Officer. 5.4 Training. Contractor shall be responsible for providing training to clinical staff/users. Training is to be scheduled in advance with the designated on-site POC. Education shall be provided prior to and/or at time of installation. Education professional shall be certified to provide instruction on the designated equipment/system. Education curriculum must include: operations and set-up, user maintenance, safety, and user troubleshooting tips. 5.5 Inspection and Acceptance. Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the on-site POC upon completion of installation. In the event deficiencies are identified, the contractor shall provide the date when the identified deficiencies will be addressed if not addressed on the date of installation. The Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the on-site POC after addressing all deficiencies. All deficiencies identified in the joint inspections shall be corrected by the Contractor prior to Government acceptance of the item. Any disputes shall be resolved by the Contracting Officer. 5.6 Deliverables. The Contractor shall provide the below documentation for the proposed equipment to VHAWASEquipmentRequests@va.gov within 10 business days of work completion: Service report. Warranty information. Electronic copy of the Operators Manual. Electronic copies of the complete technical service manuals, including troubleshooting guides, necessary diagnostic software and equipment information, schematic diagrams, and parts lists. Hours of Operation. DC VAMC s normal business hours are Monday-Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, excluding observed Federal holidays: New Year s Day Labor Day Martin Luther King s Birthday Columbus Day President s Day Veteran s Day Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day Juneteenth Christmas Day Independence Day Any other national holiday as declared by the President of the United States Period o

title: Stage 2 - Sulphur Mountain Boardwalk Repairs, Banff National Park
description: Parks Canada Agency requires the services of a qualified Contractor to complete repair work on an existing boardwalk structure located on Sulphur Mountain in Banff National Park. The boardwalk is situated in a remote environment with significant access and logistical constraints. The scope of work includes but is not limited to, structural steel member replacements and welded repairs. Access to the site is restricted to helicopter access for materials and equipment delivery and gondola access for workers. There is limited on-site staging or laydown areas, and an off-site staging area will be required for material, equipment and helicopter long line staging. Construction activities, materials, and equipment must be transported to and from the site using helicopter-supported access, requiring careful planning and coordination to safely and efficiently execute the work within a sensitive national park environment. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

title: EW038-270871-Phase 2-ITT-Construction of Sanitary Sewer Drain Pipe at Northern Forestry Centre, Edmonton
description: Late submissions will not be considered or accepted. This is Phase Two of a two-phase process. In Phase Two, only qualified suppliers in Phase-One will be invited to submit a financial bid based on the project specifications and drawings. The work consists of interior sanitary sewer repairs at the National Forestry Centre (NRCan), including installation of new sanitary sewer piping beneath the existing concrete floor, associated excavation and concrete/floor restoration, work around existing infrastructure, and site cleanup. The Contractor must complete the Work within 30 weeks of notification of acceptance of the offer. This is a secured facility. The successful contractor's personnel must be escorted on site at all times by NRCan and/or Commissionaires. The site superintendent must obtain Government of Canada Reliability security clearance before physical work begins on site. There will be an optional site visit on Tuesday, Noveber 3, 2026 at 11 A.M. Alberta Time. Interested bidders are to meet at the front desk of Northern Forestry Centre, 5320 122 Street NW, Edmonton, AB

France – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Caractérisation géotechnique du ballast
description: Dans le cadre des opérations de renouvellement de la voie ferrée, SNCF Réseau souhaite caractériser le complexe ballasté dégarni. En effet, des prélèvements en voie du ballast en vue d’une analyse de la forme géotechnique (forme du grain, dureté) sont nécessaires dans le cadre des études préliminaires des chantiers à venir. Cette prestation s’inscrit dans le projet stratégique SNCF Réseau, de valorisation des sous-produits ferroviaires et de développement du réemploi du ballast. En particulier, le cahier des charges décrit les prestations à réaliser afin d’effectuer des prélèvements des échantillons de ballast en voie et des analyses géotechniques en laboratoire, en vue de définir les conditions de réutilisation/réemploi avant réalisation de travaux. L’objectif est d’obtenir les informations suivantes sur le ballast en voie, à renouveler : -L’état de vieillissement -Les performances intrinsèques -La qualité globale La prestation à assurer est divisé en quatre missions. Ces prestations peuvent être de différentes natures et commandées indépendamment les unes aux autres : - Mission 1 : Définition du programme de prélèvement en fonction des informations transmises par le demandeur (et élaboration du devis). - Mission 2 : Réalisation des prélèvements et remise en état - Mission 3 : Conditionnement des échantillons et réalisation des analyses en laboratoire - Mission 4 : Livrables Les sites à étudier sont en exploitation ferroviaire. Le marché est alloti en 4 lots géographiques, et se présente sous forme d'un accord-cadre à bons de commande (multi-attributaires pour chaque lot). Chaque lot est conclu pour une durée ferme de 24 mois.

description: Laundry Room Sink Installation This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Kent Institution, Pacific Region. Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is open to both Indigenous and non-Indigenous businesses. All interested suppliers may participate. However, suppliers are to note that this requirement is subject to a preference for Indigenous suppliers and will be set-aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) if Canada receives two or more responsive bids from Indigenous businesses who meet the requirements of the PSIB. Indigenous businesses that have not already registered in the Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory should do so. Additional information on the Indigenous Business Directory is available at the following link: https://www.sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1100100033057/1610797769658#c3. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada requires a qualified contractor to install and commission sixteen (16) laundry sinks at Kent Institution in Agassiz, British Columbia. Objectives: To provide sixteen (16) secure, durable inmate-use sinks within the laundry rooms of the Courtyard Living Units to reduce unnecessary inmate movement between housing areas and centralized dishwashing locations and improve institutional operations, security, and staff efficiency through enhanced functionality of existing living unit spaces. Deliverables: The Contractor must: • Supply and install sixteen (16) laundry room sink stations. • Complete plumbing connections to existing domestic water and sanitary drainage systems. • Provide test and commission documentation confirming satisfactory operation of all installed plumbing systems. • Include product data sheets and warranty documentation for all major installed equipment and fixtures. • Include as-built drawings identifying any significant deviations. • Complete deficiency correction and closeout documentation as requested by CSC. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Construction Time: The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within fifteen (15) weeks from the date of notification of acceptance of the offer. File Number: 21807-27-5524015 Contracting Authority: Carlie Skotynski Telephone number: 604-756-4761 Facsimile number: 604-756-4761 E-mail: Carlie.Skotynski@csc-scc.gc.ca NOTE TO BIDDERS: Bidders can obtain the complete statement of work and evaluation criteria by downloading the solicitation document and associated documents from the Canada buys / tender opportunities website. The Crown reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada (English or French). After contract award, bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. Procurement Assistance Canada (PAC) offers seminars to businesses interested in learning how to sell goods and services to the Government of Canada. The seminars are FREE. Topics include: ? Understand the federal procurement process; ? Learn about searching for opportunities; ? Find out how to bid on opportunities; ? Discover how to prepare to sell to the government. The full schedule of seminars can be found on the Procurement Assistance Canada website, under find an event (Procurement Assistance Canada: Find an event - Canada.ca). TWO-PHASE INVITATION PROCESS This is a two-phase invitation process. Any interested supplier must refer to the special instructions to bidders. PHASE ONE: During Phase One, suppliers are invited to submit bids according to the selection procedure described below. Bidders only have to submit the Phase One documents included in this ITT. Under Phase One CSC will assess Bidders’ qualifications and experience in order to determine which bids are responsive as described under SI07 Bid Evaluation and Basis of Selection. Once Phase One bid evaluation is completed, CSC will advise bidders of whether or not their bid is responsive. PHASE TWO: During Phase Two, CSC will invite Bidders who submitted responsive bids for Phase One to submit a bid for Phase Two. Responsive Bidders will have to submit the Phase Two documents included in this ITT as part of Phase Two.

title: Sources Sought Notice: United States Naval Academy Infoblox Trinzic Equipment
description: Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled "Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes," this announcement constitutes a Sources Sought for information and planning purposes for qualified and experienced sources to provide upgrade equipment for the United States Naval Academy (USNA) Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. BACKGROUND: The United States Naval Academy (USNA) Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is responsible for developing, managing and integrating information systems and providing information technology products, services and capabilities for approximately 7,000 midshipmen, faculty and staff across the academy�s 630-acre campus and for the approximately 300 midshipmen candidates, faculty and staff at the Naval Academy Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport R.I. The proposed acquisition is to purchase equipment required to upgrade the existing, in-place USNA Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid, which provides core network naming and addressing services across USNA. The equipment purchased will replace older, like appliances that are swiftly approaching end of life and end of support by the manufacturer. The procurement will be a direct, one-for-one replacement of the 15 existing Infoblox Grid appliances; to include 10 Infoblox Trinzic X6 906 appliances, 4 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1506 appliances, and 1 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1606 appliance, along with the associated NIOS software subscriptions, Premium Maintenance-Enterprise support, power supplies, and peripheral devices required to accomplish life cycle replacement. Delivery Schedule: The anticipated Delivery schedule for this requirement will be: 30 days after receipt of order (ARO). A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Delivery / Purchase Order under NAICS Code 423430 is anticipated. NAICS CODE: The NAICS Code for this requirement is 423430, Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers, and the Small Business Size Standard is 250 (# of employees). RFI SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties shall submit responses to this Sources Sought Notice for consideration and shall include the following information (Please reference N0018927QL222 in your response) 1. Company name, address, Point of Contact name, phone number, and email address. 2. Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and DUNS Number. 3. Statement as to whether business is actively registered in the System for Award Management 4. Size of business- Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZONE, Woman-Owned and/or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business under the applicable NAICS. 5. Indicate if your company can be a prime contractor for this effort or, if not, whether your company can be a subcontractor. If subcontractors are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and if a small or large businesses will be used. 6. If the items/services can be obtained from an existing Government contract vehicle, to include, but not limited to, GSA, NASA SEWP, SeaPort-NxG, DoW ESI. Please provide the applicable contract number if available from a Government contract vehicle. 7.Capability statement displaying the offerors ability to provide the minimum requirements to include past performance information. If past performance information is provided, please include only relevant past performance on the same/similar work within the last 5 years. Please also include in past performance information the contract numbers, dollar value, and period of performance for each contract referenced in the response to this sources sought. This announcement is NOT a contract, request for proposal, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the U.S. Government. The Navy will not assume liability for costs incurred in response to this RFI. Documentation of technical expertise and experience must be presented in sufficient detail for the U.S. Government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions are not to exceed five (5) typewritten pages in no less than 12 font. All technical questions and inquiries may be submitted within the response. The Government is determining the acquisition strategy for this potential acquisition. If any potential acquisition will be a small business set-aside, then FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, applies. Note that if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small businesses, a key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a small business set-aside is that two or more potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14. If the Government determines that a small business set-aside is appropriate and your company anticipates submitting a proposal as the prime contractor for a small business set-aside, please provide specific details and rationale as to how compliance with FAR clause 52.219-14 will be achieved, including specific details regarding teaming arrangements, and if subcontracts are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of the effort to be subcontracted and whether small or large business subcontractors will be used. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. Responses should be emailed to Ms. Sheere Reese at shere.c.reese.civ@us.navy.mil by 11:00 AM eastern standard time (EST) on 19 November 2026. Again, this is not a request for a proposal. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this Sources Sought Notice. title: FCC Terre Haute condensation pumps and motor assemblies
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Complex (FCC) Terre Haute, Indiana, is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation for the requirements of 15B41827Q00000002 for condensation pumps and motor assemblies. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. This solicitation is unrestricted. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 333415. All quotes should include shipping costs, FOB destination. All products must meet the specifications of the pump and motor assemblies contained within the Statement of Work. Equivalent products may be submitted with full technical documentation for Government evaluation. It is known that the pump and motor assembly that are in place may be obsolete. It is the contractors� responsibility to best match a new assembly to meet the current specifications. All known information about the products requested can be found in the statement of work and the request for quote documents. The Government will award to the responsible offeror whose quote, conforming to the solicitation, are considered to be best value to the Government, with Price, Past Performance and Delivery time considered. Deliveries will be made to FCC Terre Haute. Located at 4700 Bureau Road South, Terre Haute, Indiana 47802 (812) 238- 1531. We will accept quotations with delivery dates past the targeted delivery date of January 28, 2026, and quotations with partial deliveries. Lead times and deliveries will be part of our evaluation process as we would prefer a single award for all items delivered on or before the targeted date. The following MUST be completed before your offer can be accepted: Representations and Certifications: Please ensure that your registration is active and up to date in the online System for Award Management. The link is www.sam.gov. Submission of your offer constitutes compliance. Standard Form (SF) 1449 - Solicitation/Contract/Order for Commercial Items. Please include your email address and UEI number in block 20. Original signatures are required on quotes submitted. The quote will be evaluated per FAR 12.203 and the government may then issue a purchase order (contract) that must be signed by both parties to complete contractual agreement. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 4.203-1(b) requires all contractors seeking or currently doing business with the government to be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award; information can be obtained at https://www.sam.gov/. All future information about this solicitation, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure they have the most up-to-date information about this solicitation. Please complete the attached Request for Quote, (RFQ) SF-1449 for submission of offers. The date for receipt of quotes is November 19th, 2026, by 11:00 AM EST. Payment will be made using Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) through a purchase order. Completed AND signed quotes must be sent electronically to C1livingston@bop.gov. Faxed bids or hand carried quotes will NOT be accepted. Thank you for your interest and if you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me by email at C1livingston@bop.gov or 812-244-4400, ext. 4476. title: J065--Notice of Intenet to Sole Source- Life Technologies Corporation Maintenance and Service for QuantStudio 12K Flex Real-Time Quantitation System
description: SPECIAL NOTICE NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE I. The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77056 in support of Central Arkansas Veterans Heath Care System (CAVHS), intends to solicit and award Sole Source, Firm-Fixed-Price, contract with a base year and four one-year ordering periods to one large business (LB) source, Life Technologies Corporation. Life Technologies Corporation. 5781 Van Allen Way Carlsbad, CA 92008 The Central Arkansas Veterans Heath care System (CAVHS) has a requirement for maintenance and repair of the following equipment: QuantStudio 12K Flex Real-Time Quantitation System Serial Number: 285881052 Associated system controller/computer, as identified in the resulting contract The equipment is located at the John L. McClellan Veterans Hospital in Little Rock, Arkansas. Required Services: The contractor shall furnish all personnel, supervision, labor, travel, transportation, tools, test equipment, replacement parts, software support, technical data, and other resources necessary to maintain the covered equipment in accordance with manufacturer operating and safety specifications. 1. Corrective maintenance and repair; 2. At least one scheduled preventive-maintenance inspection during each contract period; 3. Labor, travel, and replacement parts required for covered repairs; 4. Telephone and email technical support; 5. Remote diagnostic support through a VA-approved connection and in accordance with applicable VA information-security requirements; 6. Manufacturer-approved software, firmware, quality, safety, and field-service updates; 7. Access to proprietary diagnostic tools and technical information necessary to perform maintenance; 8. Service by qualified technicians trained to maintain the QuantStudio 12K Flex system; 9. Written service reports identifying work performed, parts installed, test equipment used, and test-equipment calibration status; and 10. Restoration of the equipment to manufacturer operating specifications following maintenance or repair. Only new original-equipment-manufacturer parts, or parts expressly approved by the manufacturer for the covered system, shall be installed. The contract price for each period shall include all covered labor, parts, travel, preventive maintenance, remote support, and technical support. Work outside the contract scope may not begin unless separately authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer through an executed contract modification. Service Levels Telephone or email acknowledgment: Within one business hours after receipt of a service request during established coverage hours. Remote diagnostics: Initiated promptly following acknowledgment of the service request. Onsite response: A qualified technician shall arrive within 4 business hours after determining that the problem cannot be resolved remotely. Service hours: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Central Time, excluding federal holidays. The anticipated contract will include a base year and four one-year ordering periods. Exercise of each ordering period will be at the sole discretion of the Government and subject to the availability of funds. II. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 811210 - Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance. Size Standard $34.0. III. This procurement is being conducted under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 12.102 (a) Restricting Competition and FAR 5.001- Notice of Proposed Contract Action. This notice is not a request for quotes, but rather a notice of intent to sole source. IV. The anticipated award date is April 18, 2027. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract. Anticipated Periods of Performance Contract Period Anticipated Dates Base Year April 18, 2027 - April 17, 2028 Option Year 1 April 18, 2028 - April 17, 2029 Option Year 2 April 18, 2029 - April 17, 2030 Option Year 3 April 18, 2030 - April 17, 2031 Option Year 4 April 18, 2031 - April 17, 2032 V. Please note that this is not a request for competitive quotes and is being posted for informational purposes only. The government does not anticipate receiving responses to this notice. However, interested parties who disagree with this action may submit a letter of interest that demonstrates your firm s technical expertise, original equipment manufacturer (OEM) authorization letter and personnel OEM training/ certifications to perform services. In addition, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the complete requirement may submit a written capability statement containing: Legal business name, physical address, Unique Entity ID, and point of contact; Business size and applicable socioeconomic status under NAICS 811210. Evidence of active registration in the System for Award Management. Evidence of authorization to service the QuantStudio 12K Flex system. Evidence that proposed technicians possess appropriate manufacturer training. Evidence of access to proprietary diagnostic tools, service software, technical documentation, updates, service bulletins, and manufacturer-approved replacement parts. Relevant experience maintaining or repairing QuantStudio 12K Flex systems. Commercially available telephone, remote, and onsite response times. Ability to begin full performance by April 18, 2027. Ability to provide continuous coverage for the base period and, if exercised, each of the four ordering periods. Identification of proposed subcontractors and the work each subcontractor would perform. A general statement of capability, reseller status, or experience with unrelated laboratory equipment will not, by itself, demonstrate the ability to satisfy the requirement. The government reserves the right to verify any request for additional documentation submitted. VI. Interested parties shall identify their interests, provide OEM authorization, personnel certifications /training as mentioned in section V of this document and capability to meet the government requirements and respond to this notice within fifteen (15) calendar days of the publication of this notice. Germany – Landscaping work for green areas – U4-Verlängerung auf die Horner Geest - Ersatzpflanzungen, Landschaftsbauarbeiten, Grünflächen und Stellplatzflächen im Abschnitt 2 [ba]
description: Die Hamburger Hochbahn baut derzeit die Verlängerung der U-Bahn-Linie U4 nach Osten, um auch den Stadtteil Horn an das U-Bahn-Netz anzuschließen. In einem ersten Bauabschnitt wurde bereits u. a. die Haltestelle Horner Rennbahn erweitert und fertiggestellt. Die Baumersatzpflanzungen und Landschaftsbauarbeiten wurden hier bereits durchgeführt. Im zweiten Bauabschnitt entsteht die neue U4-Strecke mit den Haltestellen Stoltenstraße und Horner Geest, die im Dezember 2027 in Betrieb gehen soll.. Der zweite Bauabschnitt beginnt östlich der Straße Hermannstal und folgt der Manshardtstraße nach Osten bis zur Straße Silberberg. Der U-Bahn-Tunnel wurde in offener Bauweise erstellt und verläuft zum Großteil unter der Manshardtstraße, die zurzeit wiederhergestellt wird. Die Länge dieses Abschnitts der Manshardtstraße beträgt rd. 1,6 km. Zu beiden Seiten der Manshardtstraße müssen Flächen entlang der gesamten Länge wiederhergestellt werden. Für Bewegungs- und Baustelleneinrichtungsflächen wurden seitlich der Baugrube Privatflächen, öffentliche Grünflächen und Schulhofflächen abgeräumt und in Anspruch genommen. Diese Flächen müssen ebenso wiederhergestellt werden. Die größeren wiederherzustellenden Baustelleneinrichtungs-Flächen (Bodenlager, Betonwerk und Wasseraufbereitungsanlage) befinden sich auf der Horner Rennbahn.

title: BATDOK Family of Systems (FoS)
description: Please review the full RFI document (Atch 1) for full details and instructions. A. Notice to Respondents This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e). It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Commercial Solutions Opening, and it is not a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted or for any cost incurred in responding. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not provide feedback or evaluations to individual respondents. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking proprietary information. The Government will protect properly marked information from disclosure and may share responses with Government support contractors bound by non-disclosure agreements. Do not submit classified information. B. Purpose The Defense Health Agency (DHA), Program Acquisition Executive, Medical Digital Solutions (PAE MDS), Joint Operational Medicine Information Systems (JOMIS) Program Management Office (PMO), is issuing this RFI to conduct market research for the operations and sustainment (O&S) of the Battlefield Assisted Trauma Distributed Observation Kit (BATDOK) family of systems (FoS). The anticipated period of performance begins 1 October 2027 (Fiscal Year 2028). The BATDOK FoS is comprised of BATDOK-J, an Android and iOS mobile application for point-of-injury (PoI) casualty documentation; BATDOK Link, a Windows operating system application plug-in that allows for the transfer of data from BATDOK-J into MHS GENESIS Theater (MHSG-T) or Operational Medicine Data Service (OMDS) via QR code; and BAT-TAK, a plug-in for the Android Team Awareness Kit (ATAK). The FoS is a mature capability, fielded and in operational use across the Military Services. The purpose of this RFI is to: Identify potential sources, including small businesses, with demonstrated DoW experience developing, sustaining, and integrating tactical mobile applications on the Android and iOS operating systems, together with associated ATAK and Windows plug-ins; Obtain industry input on technical approaches, best practices, and innovations for achieving the outcomes described in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) in Part II; and Inform the Government�s acquisition strategy, including contract vehicle, contract type, small business set-aside determination, and refinement of the requirement and its performance measures.

description: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Benning has a requirement to contract accommodations for 194th BDE Atlanta Lodging Holiday Block Leave Mission to support Trainee Soldiers going home for the holidays.
